content.json:
Selected windows include the start and exclude the end. Daily rates use the actual selected duration, including sub-day selections.

Volumes use decimal billing units: 1 GB = 1,000 MB = 1,000,000,000 bytes. Prices per GB and license-grant estimates use the same units. See [Microsoft Sentinel pricing and billing](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing).

Usage is reported hourly. All selected-window summaries, breakdowns, benefit-use totals and trends uniformly apportion each overlapping source hour using StartTime and EndTime; they do not measure sub-hour activity. Thus a five-minute selection uses one twelfth of an overlapping full hourly total in every view. Trends use hourly-or-coarser bins, and grant-use totals still cap eligible volume independently per UTC day. TimeGenerated is only a widened scan bound, supporting rows stamped at either boundary. Usage and history controls omit external time contexts so short selections do not truncate source-hour overlap, the 32-day commitment probe, or retained history.

> **Analytics-only model, not measured lake usage:** All lake estimates use confirmed `Plan = Analytics` Usage. Basic and Auxiliary plans and blank or unrecognized historical plans are excluded, not assumed Analytics. Missing Plan metadata can understate modeled volumes; zero does not establish zero lake usage or cost. This workbook does not verify lake onboarding or table mirroring settings; it assumes the selected Analytics data is onboarded and mirrored. Confirm those prerequisites and actual charges separately.

The data lake stores security data outside the Analytics tier and is billed on five separate meters. This workbook can estimate mirrored storage volume from workspace data, but it cannot produce a complete data lake cost estimate because several meters are not recorded in the Analytics workspace.

This section can derive the following from workspace `Usage` volume under the mirroring assumption:

- Mirrored volume size by table
- Retained raw log size based on the selected Analytics and total lake retention assumptions
- Modeled compressed log size using the documented **6:1** compression ratio
- Estimated lake storage cost for the selected time range, using the storage price parameter

The following meters are not visible in the Analytics workspace and are not modeled in this workbook:

- Data lake ingestion: monthly GB ingested into tables set to data lake tier only
- Data processing: monthly GB processed for lake-tier-only tables, including transformations such as redaction, splitting, filtering, and normalization
- Data lake query: monthly GB of uncompressed data scanned by KQL queries and jobs against the lake
- Advanced data insights: monthly notebook and job compute hours

When the data lake is enabled, Analytics-tier data can be **mirrored** to the lake at no extra ingestion charge. Workspace `Usage` provides the Analytics ingestion used as a proxy; it does not verify actual mirroring. Ingestion and data processing are charged only for tables set to **data lake tier only**; that data never reaches the Analytics workspace. Query charges depend on GB scanned and insights charges on notebook compute hours, neither of which is recorded in `Usage`.

Storage is billed on compressed data and applies only to data still retained after the Analytics retention period ends. Daily rates use the actual selected duration, including ranges shorter than one day. Each trend point uses its own covered interval, clipped at both selected edges, so a partial bucket is not divided by the duration of the entire chart. These are planning estimates, not invoice values.

Validate in **Microsoft Sentinel > Cost management** in the Microsoft Defender portal, and review the [data lake overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/datalake/sentinel-lake-overview), [billing model](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing#understand-the-full-billing-model-for-microsoft-sentinel), and [cost monitoring guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing-monitor-costs).

> **Modeled, not measured or billed:** Lake estimates use confirmed Analytics ingestion and assume mirroring; Basic, Auxiliary, and blank or unrecognized plans are excluded. The workbook does not verify onboarding or mirroring. Compressed storage assumes 6:1; other lake meters are excluded. A zero estimate does not establish zero lake use or charges.

> **Analytics-only estimate:** All six views count only nonbillable Usage with confirmed `Plan = Analytics` for the listed free sources. Basic and Auxiliary plans and blank or unrecognized historical plans are excluded, not confirmed free Analytics ingestion. The Plan field was added in May 2026; missing metadata can understate volumes, so zero does not establish that no free Analytics data was ingested. Savings use the single illustrative GB price, not actual billed discounts.

Microsoft documents the following Sentinel data sources as free:

- Azure Activity Logs (`AzureActivity`)
- Health monitoring for Microsoft Sentinel (`SentinelHealth`)
- Microsoft 365 audit activity (`OfficeActivity`)
- Microsoft Entra ID Protection alerts (`SecurityAlert`)
- Microsoft Defender for Cloud and Defender for IoT alerts (`SecurityAlert`)
- Microsoft Defender XDR incidents and alerts (`SecurityIncident`, `SecurityAlert`)
- Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, Identity, Cloud Apps, and Office 365 alerts (`SecurityAlert`)

This section estimates Analytics-tier ingestion in the selected workspace scope and keeps it separate from billable ingestion. Only nonbillable `Usage` records for these tables contribute to free volumes and savings; billable records are excluded. It does not estimate data lake-only ingestion, storage, processing, or query charges. Usage is grouped by table and cannot reliably identify the originating connector, so `SecurityAlert` cannot be allocated reliably among its contributing services. This estimate does not calculate the separate Sentinel free trial. Review the [Microsoft Sentinel free data sources](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing?tabs=simplified%2Ccommitment-tiers#free-data-sources) documentation for current eligibility and billing terms.

> **Analytics-only estimate:** Only listed tables with nonbillable Usage and confirmed Analytics plans count. Missing or unknown plans can understate volumes, so zero does not establish no free ingestion. Savings use the illustrative price, not billed discounts.

> **Analytics-only estimate:** All five Usage views count only records with `Plan = Analytics`. Basic and Auxiliary plans and blank or unrecognized historical plans are excluded, not confirmed eligible. The Plan field was added in May 2026; older or incomplete plan metadata can understate usage and savings, so zero does not establish that no eligible data was ingested.

Qualifying Microsoft 365 E7, E5, A5, F5, and G5 licenses, and corresponding Security licenses, may receive a Microsoft Sentinel data grant of up to 5 MB per qualifying user per day for eligible Microsoft 365 data.

Eligible data-source groups include:

- Microsoft Entra ID sign-in and audit logs (`SigninLogs`, `AuditLogs`, `AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs`, `AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs`, `AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs`, `AADProvisioningLogs`, `ADFSSignInLogs`, `AADUserRiskEvents`, `AADRiskyUsers`)
- Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps Guard shadow IT discovery logs (`McasShadowItReporting`)
- Microsoft Purview Information Protection logs (`InformationProtectionLogs_CL`)
- Microsoft 365 advanced hunting data (the eligible `Device*`, `Email*`, `Identity*`, `AlertEvidence`, and `CloudAppEvents` tables shown below)

This workbook estimates the Analytics-tier ingestion benefit from billable Usage data in the selected workspace scope. It does not estimate data lake-only charges or prove that a row came from an eligible connector, that the offer applies to your agreement, or that the calculated amount matches billing. The grant cap is modeled once across the selected scope for each UTC day; unused allowance does not roll over and it is not multiplied per workspace. The modeled period limit and chart lines are prorated to the selected duration; the modeled grant-used cap is also prorated on partial UTC days. This is a planning assumption, not the actual daily entitlement. Usage outside the selected range can consume the same daily allowance, so these estimates do not establish the remaining grant or the actual billed discount.

Review the [Microsoft 365 Sentinel benefit offer](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/offers/sentinel-microsoft-365-offer/) for current eligibility, agreement terms, and supported data types. Enter **Total Microsoft 365 E7/E5/A5/F5/G5 seats** below and use the global **Ingestion price** to calculate the estimate.

> **Candidate Analytics data only:** Blank or unrecognized plans are excluded, so zero does not establish ineligibility. Table usage does not prove offer or connector eligibility. The grant is modeled per UTC day, with partial days prorated; it is not actual billing.

Defender for Servers Plan 2 provides up to 500 MB of eligible ingestion per protected server or node per day. The allowance is calculated across machines in each subscription and applied at workspace level. Plan 2 must be enabled on the reporting workspace and the data must use a supported collection method. The candidate data-source groups include:

- Microsoft Defender for Cloud security alerts and recommendations (`SecurityAlert`, `SecurityBaseline`, `SecurityBaselineSummary`, `SecurityDetection`, `SecurityEvent`)
- Host protection and endpoint security data (`WindowsFirewall`, `ProtectionStatus`, `MDCFileIntegrityMonitoringEvents`)
- Defender for Endpoint custom detection data (`DeviceCustomFileEvents`, `DeviceCustomRegistryEvents`)
- Update Management data when the applicable Defender for Servers Plan 2 conditions are met (`Update`, `UpdateSummary`)

Microsoft limits the Windows security-event benefit to the `Microsoft-SecurityEvent` stream landing in `SecurityEvent`. `WindowsEvent` is excluded because `Usage` cannot verify that stream. `Usage` also cannot establish the collection method or whether `Update` and `UpdateSummary` meet the offer conditions, so the table and grant values are potentially eligible estimates, not confirmed benefits.

The entered protected-node count and candidate usage from all selected workspaces are modeled as one pool. Actual allowances are calculated by subscription and applied at workspace level, so pooling multiple scopes can overstate grant use. For a more meaningful estimate, select one matching workspace and enter its corresponding protected-node count. Grant use is capped independently for each UTC day; unused allowance does not roll over. The modeled period limit and chart lines are prorated to the selected duration; the modeled grant-used cap is also prorated on partial UTC days. This is a planning assumption, not the actual daily entitlement. Usage outside a partial-day selection can consume the same daily allowance.

The **Servers (approx.)** tile is an approximate distinct count of nonempty `Computer` hostnames reported in Heartbeat in the selected range. Hostnames can overlap or change and do not prove unique servers, licensing, or Plan 2 protection. Review the [Defender for Servers Plan 2 benefit](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/defender-for-cloud/data-ingestion-benefit) and use [reported data allocation benefits](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/fundamentals/cost-usage#view-data-allocation-benefits) or Cost Management for actual benefit use.

content.json: > **Read-only model, not measured storage or billed cost.** Uses billable Analytics Usage; unsupported or mixed plans and tables without confirmed Analytics Usage are N/A. The first-to-last observed workspace window may be shorter than the selected range; missing or idle data can skew results, and an unobserved UTC day within that window yields N/A. Assumes steady ingestion, entered included days and rates, and charges all post-Analytics days. Zero prices leave costs N/A; verify actual allowances and charges.

**Retention settings and model.** Choose one workspace and select **Configured** to use each table's current Analytics and total retention, or **What-if** to apply the entered Analytics and total days to all eligible Analytics tables. The current settings remain visible in both views. What-if total days must be at least Analytics days; no settings are changed.

The settings come from the Azure Resource Manager tables list, including inherited-setting flags, and require `Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces/tables/read`. Ingestion comes from the workspace's `Usage` table, with partial hours prorated. Its daily baseline divides by the interval between the first and last workspace Usage observations within the selected range, and displays those UTC bounds and the observed days. A shortened interval is marked as a partial Usage window. If any UTC day inside it has no workspace Usage, the model returns N/A; this also excludes genuinely inactive days. An inactive period at either edge can make the rate too high; missing records or gaps within days can make it too low. Observed endpoints and daily presence do not establish continuous or complete history. Select a representative interval and verify Usage availability. Missing settings, no confirmed Analytics sample, or mixed/unknown billable Usage plans produce N/A, not zero. The configured view cannot resolve values of -1; the What-if view can still model an eligible table using the entered days. Table names must match exactly, including case; a mismatch produces N/A. Deleted tables and retained data not represented by the API or selected Usage are excluded. Workbook results can be truncated after 10,000 rows. The displayed interactive, total and long-term days are current settings in both views; the default flags identify whether interactive days come from the workspace and total days from the interactive setting.

The selected time range bounds the observed ingestion baseline, not the retention window or a billed period. The modeled paid Analytics stock is daily billable GB times Analytics days above the included-days assumption; modeled long-term stock is daily billable GB times total minus Analytics days. Monthly cost multiplies each modeled stock by its entered GB/month rate. Enter USD rates for the workspace region; no currency conversion is performed. This illustration assumes all long-term days are chargeable; actual allowances, prices, historical ingestion, plan changes, and storage may differ. Sentinel data lake and XDR meters are separate. Use [Cost Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/quick-acm-cost-analysis) for actual charges and review [retention settings](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/data-retention-configure).

**Scans are off by default.** Expanding this section does not enable any retention query. Read the cost warning, review the selected workspaces, and explicitly set **Run retention scans** to **Yes - enable potentially chargeable scans** to show and execute the three queries. Set it back to **No** to hide them and stop further refreshes; this does not cancel already submitted requests.

**Limited accessible-data estimate, not the complete retention bill.** These queries apply the entered price to billable records older than 90 days that ordinary queries can access. Plans, retention periods, included retention, and prices vary by table; 90 days is only this estimate's cutoff, not proof that each returned record incurs a retention charge.

Ordinary queries generally cannot retrieve Analytics or Basic long-term-retained data without search jobs; Auxiliary data may remain queryable for its full retention period. These legacy scans do not run search jobs or use table retention settings. Missing or inaccessible history makes retention cost **unknown**, not zero, and even populated results are incomplete. See [Log Analytics data retention and query limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/data-retention-configure).

**Query cost and performance:** The three wildcard scans can be expensive across large workspaces and may incur scan charges for Basic or Auxiliary tables, or encounter unsupported-query restrictions. Once explicitly enabled, they omit external time contexts to preserve accessible history older than the cutoff; the selected range only scales the period estimate. Review scope and query charges before enabling or refreshing.

Use [Cost Management cost analysis](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/quick-acm-cost-analysis) and each table's retention settings for actual charges. XDR and data lake retention use separate billing models; see [Manage data tiers and retention in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/manage-data-overview).

> **Potentially chargeable scans:** Off by default. Enabling or refreshing may cause expensive wildcard scans and Basic or Auxiliary scan charges; turning them off stops future refreshes, not submitted requests. Estimates cover accessible billable records older than 90 days, not the retention bill; plans and retention vary by table. Inaccessible history is unknown, not zero; search jobs and table settings are not used in these scans. Verify actual costs in [Cost Management](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/quick-acm-cost-analysis) and review [retention limits](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/data-retention-configure).

Microsoft Sentinel and Log Analytics offer Pay-As-You-Go and Commitment Tier pricing. Select one **Commitment tier workspace** below to read its **Log Analytics workspace SKU** and compare its average billable Analytics-plan daily ingestion over the last 31 days with listed volume levels. Both SKU detection and usage history are scoped only to this workspace, independently of the global workspace and time-range filters. Changing this selector does not change other workbook sections.

The initial selection prefers a workspace selected in the global filter, ordered by workspace name and resource ID. When the global filter selects all workspaces, the first accessible Sentinel workspace in that order is selected. This is a default, not an inferred primary workspace; use the dropdown to choose the workspace you want to evaluate. If no accessible Sentinel workspace is found, check your subscriptions and permissions.

> **Detected SKU is not a detected Sentinel tier:** The query reads only the Log Analytics workspace SKU. It does not determine the Sentinel pricing mode or tier, promotional eligibility, negotiated rates, or dedicated-cluster billing. Classic Sentinel and Log Analytics tiers can differ; simplified pricing combines their meters, and dedicated-cluster billing can depend on cluster settings. Verify the actual configuration using [Microsoft Sentinel pricing tiers](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/enroll-simplified-pricing-tier) and the portal before comparing prices or changing tiers.

> **50 GB/day promotional tier:** Microsoft documents a promotional offer through December 31, 2026, with customers able to lock promotional pricing through March 31, 2027. Eligibility, regional pricing, discounts, later tier availability, and any existing price lock are not verified here. The 50 GB/day comparison is a volume reference, not a claim that the tier or promotional offer is available now. Review the [promotion announcement and eligibility guidance](https://learn.microsoft.com/partner-center/announcements/2026-june#sentinel-50-gb-tier-promo-extended). Usage below 100 GB/day does not establish that Pay-As-You-Go is the appropriate pricing option.

> **Plan and history scope:** The query omits an external timespan and uses a widened TimeGenerated scan for the full 32-day history probe. Source hours and the 31-day volume use StartTime. Basic and Auxiliary usage are excluded. Blank or unrecognized Usage plans within the 31-day review window are reported in **Unknown-plan Usage rows** and withhold both the average and volume comparison, rather than being assumed Analytics or silently ignored.

> **New workspace notice:** A volume comparison is shown only after 31 days of billable Analytics-plan history are detected. Until then, the table reports how many days remain; a shorter history cannot accurately represent the fixed 31-day review period.

> **Volume comparison only, not a pricing recommendation:** **Volume ceiling** is the smallest listed level at or above the unrounded average, not a recommended purchase or a claim of eligibility. The displayed average is rounded to two decimal places. The comparison does not account for commitment prices, overage, discounts, or Pay-As-You-Go costs; a lower tier with overage may cost less. The workbook cannot establish pricing alignment with the detected Log Analytics SKU. Review [Usage and estimated costs in the Azure portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/change-pricing-tier#changing-pricing-tier) using your applicable pricing before changing a tier.

Review **Days since tier last changed** before making a change: a commitment tier has a 31-day period during which it cannot move to a lower commitment or consumption tier. Confirm rates on the [Microsoft Sentinel pricing page](https://www.microsoft.com/security/pricing/microsoft-sentinel/) and review [Plan costs and understand pricing and billing for Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/billing?tabs=simplified%2Ccommitment-tiers#analytics-tier).

> **Volume comparison only, not a pricing recommendation:** The detected value is the Log Analytics workspace SKU, not a verified Sentinel tier or classic/simplified pricing mode; cluster billing is not checked. Microsoft documents the 50 GB/day promotion through December 31, 2026 and a price lock through March 31, 2027; eligibility, pricing, and current tier availability are unverified. Below-100 GB/day usage does not imply Pay-As-You-Go. The ceiling uses the unrounded average; the displayed average is rounded. Unknown plans or insufficient history withhold the comparison. Verify Sentinel pricing, offer terms, and 31-day commitment restrictions in the portal.

parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'Microsoft.operationsmanagement/solutions'
| where name contains 'SecurityInsights'
| extend workspaceResourceId = tolower(tostring(properties.workspaceResourceId))
| summarize by workspaceResourceId
| join kind=inner (resources | where type =~ 'Microsoft.OperationalInsights/workspaces' | project workspaceResourceId = tolower(id), workspaceName = name) on workspaceResourceId
| extend preference = iif(workspaceResourceId in~ ({Workspace}), 0, 1)
| order by preference asc, workspaceName asc, workspaceResourceId asc
| project value = workspaceResourceId, label = workspaceName, selected = true

parameters.name: CurrentCommitmentTier
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.operationalinsights/workspaces'
| where id =~ '{CommitmentWorkspace}'
| extend skuName = tolower(tostring(properties.sku.name)), capacityReservationLevel = toint(properties.sku.capacityReservationLevel)
| extend currentTier = case(skuName == 'capacityreservation' and capacityReservationLevel > 0, strcat(tostring(capacityReservationLevel), ' GB/day capacity reservation'), skuName == 'capacityreservation', 'Capacity reservation - level unavailable', skuName == 'pergb2018', 'Pay-As-You-Go', skuName == 'free', 'Free tier', skuName == 'standalone', 'Standalone tier', skuName == 'standard', 'Standard tier', skuName == 'premium', 'Premium tier', 'Unknown')
| summarize WorkspaceCount = dcount(id), CurrentTier = any(currentTier)
| project CurrentCommitmentTier = case(WorkspaceCount == 1, CurrentTier, WorkspaceCount == 0, 'Not available', 'Multiple workspaces')

content.query: let reviewDays = 31.0; let reviewStart = ago(31d); let historyProbeStart = ago(32d); let currentTier = '{CurrentCommitmentTier}'; let tierLevels = dynamic([50,100,200,300,400,500,1000,2000,5000]); Usage | where TimeGenerated >= historyProbeStart - 1h and TimeGenerated < now() + 1h | where StartTime >= historyProbeStart and StartTime < now() | where IsBillable == true | extend UsagePlan = tostring(column_ifexists('Plan', '')) | summarize TotalBilledMB = sumif(Quantity, StartTime >= reviewStart and UsagePlan =~ 'Analytics'), FirstObserved = minif(StartTime, UsagePlan =~ 'Analytics'), UnknownPlanRows = countif(StartTime >= reviewStart and UsagePlan !in~ ('Analytics', 'Basic', 'Auxiliary')) | extend ObservedHistoryDays = iif(isnull(FirstObserved), 0.0, min_of(reviewDays, datetime_diff('second', now(), FirstObserved) / 86400.0)) | extend DaysRemaining = toint(ceiling(max_of(reviewDays - ObservedHistoryDays, 0.0))) | extend AvgDailyGB = iif(DaysRemaining == 0 and UnknownPlanRows == 0, TotalBilledMB / 1000.0 / reviewDays, real(null)), TierLevels = tierLevels | mv-expand TierLevel = TierLevels to typeof(int) | extend CoversAverage = TierLevel >= AvgDailyGB | summarize VolumeCeilingGBPerDay = minif(TierLevel, CoversAverage), AvgDailyGB = any(AvgDailyGB), ObservedHistoryDays = any(ObservedHistoryDays), DaysRemaining = any(DaysRemaining), UnknownPlanRows = any(UnknownPlanRows) | extend volumeCeiling = case(currentTier == 'Multiple workspaces', 'Not evaluated', UnknownPlanRows > 0, 'Not evaluated - unknown Usage plan', DaysRemaining > 0, strcat('Ready in ', tostring(DaysRemaining), iif(DaysRemaining == 1, ' day', ' days')), AvgDailyGB == 0.0, 'No billable Analytics volume', VolumeCeilingGBPerDay == 50, '50 GB/day - verify availability', isnotnull(VolumeCeilingGBPerDay), strcat(tostring(VolumeCeilingGBPerDay), ' GB/day'), 'Above listed 5000 GB/day - check portal') | extend offerStatus = 'Promo through 2026-12-31; lock through 2027-03-31 - verify' | extend reviewStatus = case(currentTier == 'Multiple workspaces', 'Not evaluated', UnknownPlanRows > 0, 'Plan data unavailable', DaysRemaining > 0, 'Not Ready', 'Verify in portal') | project ['Log Analytics tier'] = currentTier, ['Volume ceiling'] = volumeCeiling, ['50 GB/day offer'] = offerStatus, Status = reviewStatus, ['Avg daily GB'] = round(AvgDailyGB, 2), ['Unknown-plan Usage rows'] = UnknownPlanRows

Microsoft Sentinel playbooks use Azure Logic Apps to automate responses to incidents, alerts, and other security operations workflows. This section discovers accessible **Consumption Logic Apps** (`microsoft.logic/workflows`) across the selected subscription and resource group scope. It does not discover Standard Logic Apps hosted as `microsoft.web/sites`, and matching resources are not necessarily Sentinel playbooks.

All matching Consumption Logic Apps are included by default. Use the subscription, resource group, and Logic Apps controls to narrow the scope. The table below is a current resource inventory, not historical execution or billing data.

**Usage reporting:** Azure Monitor platform metrics can provide runs, failures, billable actions, and billable triggers by Logic App over the selected time range. Azure Workbooks supports a native **Metrics** data source that can display these in charts or grids without querying the `AzureMetrics` log table. When exported metrics are stored in a Basic or Auxiliary table, the Analytics Logs query path is not appropriate; the separate Logs (Basic) data source has query costs and limitations. Neither metrics availability nor workbook data-source support is established by this inventory. Review the [Workbook data sources](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/visualize/workbooks-data-sources) and [Logic Apps metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/reference/supported-metrics/microsoft-logic-workflows-metrics).

**Cost reporting:** Billable execution counts are usage measures, not currency. A Consumption cost illustration needs the applicable built-in, standard-connector, enterprise-connector, and storage rates and allowances. Standard Logic Apps additionally have hosting and separately billed storage costs. For actual or amortized costs, use Cost Management data grouped by resource ID, date, meter, and currency, including related hosting and storage resources. Missing metrics or costs should be reported as unavailable, not zero. See [Logic Apps billing](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/logic-apps/logic-apps-pricing) and [cost monitoring and exports](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/logic-apps/plan-manage-costs).

**Overall totals:** Do not add the existing workbook sections together as an invoice estimate: some are subsets of the same ingestion, some are hypothetical savings, and others are storage projections. A combined cost view needs one consistent scope, period, currency, and cost basis, without duplicated benefit, hosting, or storage charges. Usage quantities such as GB, executions, and hosting hours must remain separate.

Review [Automate threat response with playbooks in Microsoft Sentinel](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/sentinel/automation/automate-responses-with-playbooks) for playbook guidance. Because playbooks use Azure Logic Apps, additional charges can apply. Go to the [Azure Logic Apps](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/logic-apps/) pricing page for more details.

> **Inventory only:** Shows current Consumption Logic Apps, not necessarily Sentinel playbooks; Standard apps, runs, usage, and actual charges are not shown. Logic Apps may incur charges. Do not add workbook sections into an invoice total: ingestion subsets, hypothetical savings, and storage projections can overlap.
